# Test fixtures

Provenance of everything in this directory, because a published repository
should say where its images came from.

| file | what it is | origin |
|---|---|---|
| `stress.png` | A precision pattern of the cases that break centreline tracing: crossings at 90° and 15°, T-junctions, corners, cusps, lone loops, parallel lines at 1×/2×/4× the stroke gap, three stroke weights, a filled triangle, dashes, dots, a tight spiral, dense hatching, a tapering stroke, concentric and tangent circles, nested ridges, a long shallow arc. Each specimen is isolated so a failure can be attributed. | Generated by `examples/make_stress.py`. Rebuild it any time. |
| `beach.png` | A beach scene: flat colour regions (sand, sea, a red-and-white ball) under black line work, with fine hatching on the towel and stipple on the sand. It is the repository's lead example, and the hardest case here — the sand and sea are *fills*, not strokes, and there are four inks to separate. | Generated with ChatGPT as line art, then traced by this tool into SVG. |
| `polymerase.png` | Line art of a DNA polymerase — a single closed contour with about sixty scallops, drawn in blue on white. It is the compact counter-example to `beach.png`: a whole drawing that comes out as one path of 97 curves, 3.8 KB from 777 KB. | Generated with ChatGPT as line art, then traced by this tool into SVG. |

`lineart_trace.corpus` holds the rest of the test material — 40 labelled
specimens built in code, so they need no files and can be regenerated exactly.
Write them out as PNGs with `python examples/make_corpus.py out/`.

## Adding your own

Drop any drawing in here and the benchmark picks it up automatically, scored
against its own ink:

```bash
python examples/benchmark.py
```

To have the test suite cover it too, add a floor for it in
`tests/test_fixtures.py`. Anything named there but absent is skipped, so the
suite still passes on a clean checkout.
